text: Buzz--Buzz--Buzz... Buzz--Buzz--Buzz--
While experiencing the familiar sensation of sleeping, I hear something vibrating in a familiar rhythm.
I roll over and begin to think about a question in a daze: Would a young Jyanshi keep dreaming about something they don't want to face in reality?
However, the vibration sound that just doesn't stop makes me gradually realize that I might not be dreaming. Someone really is calling me today, and this person is also very persistent.
I get up sleepily and look at the caller ID. It is an unknown number.
I pick up the call, but the other person hangs up before I can say anything. After listening to the "beep... beep... beep..." busy tone, I receive a text message.
Unknown Number
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) We'll meet up at Countless Springs at 6:43.

The text message is attached with a route map. To be precise, it looks like a route map customized to give me directions to go to Countless Springs. Every traffic transfer point is marked, and even the walking time has been set out for me. For example: "Walk from Line 1 of the subway to Line 10 in six minutes."

At the bottom of the route map are some words highlighted in red: "Don't take a taxi. There are a total of five routes that taxis can use to go to Countless Springs, and they are ALL CONGESTED WITH TRAFFIC!

Given what I've been up to recently, I'm pretty sure that Strix sent me this text message. I don't even think it's strange that they know my mobile phone number. After all, I've been getting sales calls for real estate, educational institutions, and bank loans... I've even received countless calls from dating agencies, which gives me the illusion that the whole world knows my mobile phone number.

However, it's only 6 a.m. right now. When I searched Countless Springs's business hours online, I saw that it only opens at 10 a.m. every morning. Is it really necessary for me to go there so early in the morning?

I mention my doubts in my reply to the text message and receive another reply almost instantly. I received a photo that looks like it was taken on the street where Countless Springs is located. Probably due to the height of the person taking the photograph, all I can see in the photo are the heads of many people. Even so, I can vaguely tell that this photo was taken by someone in a queue.

Suddenly, I remember reading online that Countless Springs will open up its garden to the public on the day of the auction. Geisha performances and interactive activities will also be held at fixed times during the day, so it is usually packed with people on the day. To enter the venue early, many people even start lining up on the previous day and wait all night.
It looks like I will really need to go out soon. I wash up quickly and check that the precious bank card is packed safely in my bag before I leave the house.

On my way to the exit of my apartment building, I receive another text message, which is a row filled with ellipses without anything else. However, I can feel that this message is conveying feelings such as silence, speechlessness, and frustration. Thanks to my years of experience in chatting online, I quickly understand the real meaning of these punctuation marks.
I start receiving about one text message every 30 seconds on average. I check them one by one.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) ....................................
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) You're so slow.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) You left home late because of your meaningless doubts. The route you received earlier no longer applies because the traffic situation has changed.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) This is your new route. I hope you will follow it precisely this time! If you do, you will arrive at your destination at 7:26.

I start running towards the nearest subway station while opening the new route map. Is this the strength of an intelligence organization? Somehow, they know that I had only just left home! Where could the surveillance camera that betrayed my whereabouts possibly be?

Although the morning rush of Line 1 isn't so crazy that station attendants would need to push people into the train, it's still crowded enough to make it difficult to get on the train and even more difficult to get off. By the time you finally push through the crowd to reach the door of the train, you usually get pushed back into the depths of the train by a stream of people who are eager to get inside.

After experiencing this a few times, I finally manage to squeeze out of the train at the last second when the lights are flashing. I take a look at the route map for the next stop. I need to run from Line 1 to Line 9 within six minutes and thirty seconds.
The subway station is filled with silence today.

Anyone who has taken the train in One Han City would know that the transfer route between Line 1 and Line 9 is one of the three "subway legends." Even though it is only 600 meters on foot, it usually takes more than ten minutes by foot because you need to get through everyone in your way, which means I'll need to put in some real effort to get to Line 9 within six minutes and thirty seconds.

I look at my mobile phone and realize that I don't have much time left. After thinking for five seconds, I decide to go for it. Fortunately, I won't need to put in the effort required for a 1,000-meter sprint like in a physical fitness test.

I manage to rush inside the train of Line 9 just as the lights on the door start to flash, indicating that the train is about to start. It seems that the time has been calculated very precisely on this route map, factoring in the time each transport tool stops at stations, as well as the limits of my athletic ability...
I don't understand how it can be accurate to the second!

After a bumpy ride, I finally exit the subway station. I then walk a certain distance and arrive at the street where Countless Springs is located. The time is 7:29. I didn't manage to arrive at the exact time predicted by the route map, but I tried my best.

In front of me is a queue just as long as a queue for an anime convention. It extends all the way around the corner and back again. Although I'm only ten meters away from the entrance of Countless Springs, it'll be a long time before I can get inside.

The longest distance in the world isn't the distance between the edge of the sky and the rim of the sea, nor being on different servers in the same game, but the distance between a person at the front and the back of a queue because you might already be outside by the time I finally get in.
As I ruefully lament about the length of the line, my mobile phone starts vibrating, and a message notification pops up.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) Look towards your eleven o'clock direction after fifteen minutes.

I look up but don't see anyone familiar around me, so I follow the instructions in the text message and stay where I am. While waiting patiently for the time to pass, I look through the photos of the pool party shared by the members of Asaha High School in CatChat... After fifteen minutes, my mobile phone vibrates again, but there is only one punctuation mark this time.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) !
I look up knowingly and see Noah waving to me with a mobile phone in her hand. A familiar figure, one of the "statues" in Kutsuji's office that day, is standing next to her.
After seeing me, the "statue" runs over and hands me a bag he was holding while pushing me into the place where he was standing. Only then do I realize that he was lining up for me.
I open the bag in my hand and find a piping hot breakfast. Noah purses her lips as she taps her mobile phone quickly for a moment. My mobile phone starts vibrating immediately after that.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) Eat this food while you can. You won't get to eat anything after you enter at 8:00.
So she's the one who has been sending me text messages! Why is she telling me that I won't get to eat anything after I enter?
Just as I raise my head and prepare to ask her about it, I see a sign at the door that says: "No food is allowed inside during the auction."

I find myself beginning to believe what Kutsuji told me. Noah doesn't like to talk, but she excels at everything else. It would be perfect if she can talk to me instead of texting me when we are face to face...
I pat my stomach and feel happy that I have a little something to eat so I won't get too hungry. Noah pats my arm, then takes out two tickets and gives me one of them.
Seeing that she is about to write me another text message on her mobile phone, I quickly stop her and nod my head.
player
{character:player}I can see that these are tickets you prepared in advance.
She nods at me blankly and leads me to the ticket office at the entrance.
It looks like it's more difficult to get along with this child than I thought.
"For your safety and the safety of others, please don't run inside the subway station."
"Please be careful and avoid looking down at your mobile phone while using the escalator."

The loudspeaker hanging on the handrail at the entrance of the escalator is playing pre-recorded warnings in a loop. In my head, I see myself being stopped and dissuaded by a station attendant, so I feel like this option isn't feasible. What's more, I feel like my body doesn't want to run like this either...

{character:player}It's okay, I still have time. Based on my experience of lining up for anime conventions, the best option isn't to start lining up the night before but to enter without lining up at noon when almost everyone has already gone inside.

I comfort myself in my heart as I walk to Line 9 and arrive just in time to see the doors of the train of Line 9 close. The train starts, and the electronic screen on the platform tells me that the next train will arrive at the station in five minutes...
After sighing, I look through the photos of the pool party shared by the members of Asaha High School on CatChat while I wait patiently for the time to pass.

It isn't long before another text message notification pops up on my mobile phone. After opening it, I see another route map, but it is mostly the same since I am already two-thirds of the way there. The arrival time on the new route map is now 7:54, and there are some words highlighted in red at the bottom: "Be prepared to be hungry."
Why should I be prepared to be hungry if I'm late? Did I miss some important clues along the way? Since the train hasn't arrived yet, I send a reply with my questions.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) It's because you need to order one month in advance for lunch at Countless Springs today, but obviously you didn't do so.
It's sobering to see something so realistic early in the morning.
But I checked the new route map. Even if I'm a few minutes late at each step, I shouldn't be half an hour late, right?
This question is solved soon after I leave the subway station.
The exit closest to Countless Springs has been cordoned off, and a group of children wearing yellow hats pass by in front of me one after another.

According to the conversations of passers-by, a nearby elementary school has organized a spring outing today, so this area will be blocked off for fifteen minutes for their safety when they pass through the area.

I look at the other exits of the subway station and realize that they are either very far away from my destination, or I will need to go through an intersection with a set of traffic lights that take ages to change. After comparing the options repeatedly, I find that the fastest option is to stay here and wait.

It's almost 8:00 by the time I approach my destination. I rush to the entrance of Countless Springs, and before I can express my shock at how long the line in front of me is, I am pushed to the front of the line by a person who looks a little familiar. Noah is standing next to him with an unhappy expression on her face.

The mood is a bit low. After I greet her awkwardly, I am guided to the ticket office. Suddenly, my stomach starts rumbling loudly, which makes everyone fall silent around me for a while. Noah and everyone else look at me in unison... What I'm afraid of the most is that everyone will become silent because of this embarrassing situation.

Although it isn't long before everyone does their own thing again like nothing happened, I can't pretend that nothing happened. After waking so early in the morning and experiencing such strenuous exercise, I can feel myself getting hungrier. I hope I don't make any strange noises during the auction later...

I look back at the person who changed places with me just now. The reason I find him familiar is that he was one of the "statues" in Kutsuji's office yesterday. I watch as he takes a sandwich out of a bag he is carrying in his hands, shows it to me, and then puts it in his mouth...
If I'm not mistaken, that should be my breakfast. I look up at the warning sign at the entrance: "No food is allowed inside during the auction."
At this moment, I have a deeper understanding of the message: "Be prepared to be hungry."
Because I arrived late, I wouldn't need to line up for very long, and Strix prepared a ticket for me in advance. Noah gave me one, which let me know that today's task had started officially.
Strix must be good at what it does since its information network is so massive. There must be a reason why the route map is like this.

Moreover, I remember reading online that Countless Springs will open up its garden to the public on the day of the auction. Geisha performances and interactive activities will also be held at fixed times during the day, so it is usually packed with people on the day. To enter the venue early, many people even start lining up on the previous day and wait all night.
So I follow its instructions and get up to leave immediately.

While following the route map, I realize that the arrival times of the train at each station are accurate to the second. As long as I follow its instructions, I should be able to get on the train after transferring at each station, as well as arrive at each intersection in time to cross the road with a green light.
It is exactly 6:43 by the time I arrive at the destination. The accuracy of the calculation is simply stunning.

However, the smooth part of my journey has ended. After arriving at the entrance of Countless Springs, I find out that I can't enter it directly. In front of me is an S-shaped queue that extends all the way around the corner and back again. Although I'm only ten meters away from the entrance of Countless Springs, it'll be a long time before I can get inside.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) Look towards your eleven o'clock direction.
I look over subconsciously and see Noah motioning at me with her mobile phone in the air. A familiar figure, one of the "statues" in Kutsuji's office yesterday, is standing next to her.
After seeing me, he runs over and hands me a bag he was holding while pushing me into the place where he was standing. Only then do I realize that he was lining up for me.
I open the bag in my hand and find a piping hot breakfast. Noah purses her lips as she taps her mobile phone quickly for a moment. My mobile phone starts vibrating immediately after that.
So she's the one who has been sending me text messages. Why is she telling me that I won't get to eat anything after I enter?
Just as I raise my head and prepare to ask her about it, I see a sign at the door that says: "No food is allowed inside during the auction."
After I eat breakfast in a leisurely manner, it doesn't take long before it's our turn to enter. Noah pats my arm, then takes out two tickets and gives me one of them.
She looks at me with slightly raised lips like she is smiling, but then she turns her head immediately and leads me to the ticket office at the entrance.
I'm not really sure of what happened because everything happened so quickly. Did she really smile just now? Is she a little tsundere?!

After our tickets are checked, we follow the stream of people through the entrance of Countless Springs. Those who will take part in the auction will be separated from the other visitors at the first fork and go to a special venue for the auction.

After walking through a labyrinth of winding corridors, we finally arrive at a hall filled with flowers. Some vine-like flowers have climbed all over the vermilion-colored pillars here, infusing the venue with a spring aura.

However, the flowers used for decoration are all common varieties. According to information that Noah, who is like a walking encyclopedia, sends to me via text messages, the cut flowers that will be sold in the auction are extremely rare varieties that Countless Springs has grown with meticulous care. For example, the flowers that will be auctioned in the auction we'll take part in are flowing gold camellia, coral red skimmia, and snow tower peony.

When I pick up the auction guide on the seat and browse through it, I learn that the auction format adopted by Countless Springs is unlike the format used by other common auctions. It is a "sellers' call auction," which is also known more simply as a Dutch auction.

In this type of auction, the auctioneer starts by quoting the highest price, and then buyers start bidding. If there are no bids, the auctioneer will lower the price until someone buys the item or the item isn't sold because it falls below the minimum price set by the client in advance.

If two or more buyers place bids during this time, the auctioneer will state a new price in increasing order, and the auction becomes the more common ascending auction, in which the price keeps increasing until no one increases the price further.

We sit in our designated seats and wait for the auction to start. Since Noah is still sending text messages to me next to me, my mobile phone keeps vibrating, which makes the people around me look at my pocket with strange eyes.
I sigh, then I take out my phone and continue to read the messages she has sent to me.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) Although many people come every time, most of them are hoping to get lucky and take this opportunity to have afternoon tea with Kurone Toujou.

{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) According to the intelligence, Kurone Toujou hasn't performed any dances or shamisen music for many years now, but she is one of the Four Greats after all, and her admirers will try to see her in person no matter what.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) So you need to get the timing right after the auction starts.
This information makes me uneasy.
{character:player}(Text message) Is there enough money in this black card? Is it possible that I won't have enough money to pay after I make a bid?
Noah looks up and glances at me. The look of surprise and contempt makes me very certain that I'm worrying about nothing as Kutsuji should be very rich.

{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) You'll be able to spend up to 10 million Coppers with this card, which is an estimate of the cost based on the final price paid for the cut flowers in previous auctions. There are no records of any cut flowers being sold for more than this amount.
As I expected, I was worrying about nothing. I just know that Kutsuji is much better at making money than me because I would at least blush when I'm not in the right.
When did I start sending text messages too instead of talking in person? I can only say that social anxiety disorder is a transmittable phenomenon.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) Of course, I can't guarantee that no accidents will happen today, so please be vigilant.
At the same time Noah sends me that text message reminder, she also hands me a number plate with the number 17 on it.
{character:Unknown Number}This is your auction number. Hold onto it and raise it when you need to make a bid later.
{character:player}(Text message) Okay.
{character:player}(Text message) I have a question to ask you.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) What is it? The auction is starting soon.

{character:player}(Text message) Why do you end every sentence in your text messages with a punctuation mark? You're making me check whether I have a punctuation mark at the end of my messages too before I send them.
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) ...
{character:player}(Text message) ...
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) That has nothing to do with you.
{character:player}(Text message) Oh
System notification: {var:player_nickname} recalled a message.
{character:player}(Text message) Oh.

The seats around me start to fill up, and the sound of a gong announces the start of the auction. I look at where the sound is coming from and see a golden gong on one side of the auction stand. The whole auction hall falls silent immediately after the gong is sounded, kind of like how high school students in self-study class fall silent when they see their head teacher's face in the window of the back door.

The auctioneer of Countless Springs, a woman with a charming figure and a pipe hanging from her waist, sways gently as she walks slowly onto the stage. Judging from the respectful attitude of the people around her, she should be the one in charge here. After taking to the stage, she claps her hands, summoning three flower-bearing girls to the front of the stage.

{character:Auctioneer}This time, we will be auctioning three arrangements of cut flowers, namely flowing gold camellia, coral red skimmia, and snow tower peony. Countless Springs carefully cultivated these varieties, and you can admire their beauty first.

As she speaks, the three flower-bearing girls walk past us slowly one by one from the stand in the middle. Their pace is measured, giving us just enough time to see the cut flowers in their hands clearly.

The first arrangement is the flowing gold camellia, which features several globe-shaped golden camellia flowers the size of a baby's fist surrounded by silver-white baby's breath flowers that are like stars around the moon. When the girl takes the flowers to the window, I see flowing light passing by after the sun shines on the petals, I instantly understand why it is named flowing gold camellia.

The second arrangement is the coral red skimmia. Skimmia isn't an easy plant to cultivate, and this arrangement is like a precious gem that is even more translucent than ordinary skimmia flowers. Instead of being decorated with unnecessary flowers, this arrangement features a large number of monstera deliciosa leaves laid out on all sides with snow-colored dusty miller flowers in the middle. On top of the dusty miller flowers, coral red skimmia blossoms that look like bright red corals are scattered everywhere like red agate on the snow.

The third arrangement features two huge snowy peonies, which seem to be grown as a pair. According to my rough estimate, these two flowers have a diameter of about 17 centimeters and a height of nearly 10 centimeters, making them true kings among flowers. Their petals are silvery-white like snow, and you can see bright yellow stamens at the bottom of the slightly pale pink petals in the middle. Set with eucalyptus leaves as their backdrop, this arrangement has an unworldly air of elegance.
After showing everyone the cut flowers, the three girls return to the stage and stand next to each other.
{character:Auctioneer}We will now start, and you will have fifteen minutes of thinking time. After that, we'll start the auction for the flowing gold camellia.
{character:player}(Text message) Does this mean that it's pointless for me to bid on the two other arrangements if I manage to win the auction for the first arrangement?
{character:player}(Text message) ?
{character:Unknown Number}(Text message) I can see your screen...
I pause for a moment. Under her silent gaze, I add her contact and input her name.
{character:player}(Text message) I have an idea. Why don't we each bid on one arrangement to increase our chances of success?

{character:Noah}(Text message) No. It isn't easy to become eligible to participate in the auction, and we only managed to get the number plate you're holding after putting in a lot of effort over a long time.
{character:player}(Text message) Give me a hint then. For example, can you tell me which flower arrangement to bid on?
{character:Noah}(Text message) Didn't the boss tell you yesterday? It's a mystery draw, and there are no observable rules. Just do what you usually do when you bet your chance on an Ura Dora.
In that case, I'll choose...
I choose the first arrangement, the flowing gold camellia. Noah does not object to my decision.
The auction has started officially. I clench the number plate in my hand nervously. To my surprise, the auctioneer starts off with a price that takes everyone's breath away: 50 million Coppers.
{character:Noah}(Text message) Show some composure and don't panic. This is normal.

{character:Noah}(Text message) Everyone here has done their own investigations. In most cases, very few people would make a bid until the price falls within the normal price range. Last year, the flowing gold camellia sold for 6.5 million Coppers.
I look around me and see that while some people are intimidated by the price like me, quite a few people are quite calm. She is right though, and no one raises their number plate yet.
The auctioneer takes the hint and continues to lower the price. 40 million Coppers... 30 million Coppers... The price has dropped to 10 million Coppers, but nobody has raised their number plate yet.
Recalling that the bank card has exactly 10 million Coppers in it, I start to consider making a bid...
The lower the price, the greater the competition I'll face and the greater the risk... Maybe I should get this now since it looks like Kutsuji is rich enough that he probably doesn't care.
With this thought in mind, I decisively raise my number plate. The auctioneer looks at me and starts calling out the bid after nodding at me.
Auctioneer
{character:Auctioneer}10 million Coppers going once.
{character:Auctioneer}10 million Coppers going twice.
{character:Auctioneer}10 million Coppers going three times.
{character:Auctioneer}The flowing gold camellia has been sold at the price of 10 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.17.
The crisp sound of the mallet announces my success, but before I can share my joy with Noah, I hear a sigh next to me.
Noah
{character:Noah}(Text message) You're a goner.

Since Noah said this flower was sold for 6.5 million Coppers last year, it's unlikely that anyone will buy it at the current price this year. I think everyone will wait until the price falls within a suitable range before bidding on it.
I wait patiently for the countdown to end. As I expected, no one raises their number plate, and the auctioneer continues to lower the price. 9 million Coppers... 8 million Coppers...

Now's the time to start bidding. Since it sold for 6.5 million Coppers before, 8 million Coppers is already in the bidding range. It'll only become riskier and more people will start competing if the price drops further. I decisively raise my number plate. The auctioneer looks at me and starts calling out the bid after nodding at me.
{character:Auctioneer}8 million Coppers going once.
{character:Auctioneer}8 million Coppers going twice.
{character:Auctioneer}8 million Coppers going three times.
{character:Auctioneer}The flowing gold camellia has been sold at the price of 8 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.17.
The crisp sound of the mallet announces my success, but before I can share my joy with Noah, she frowns and thinks for a while before talking to me.
{character:Noah}(Text message) I guess it's okay.

This kind of auction is like a big gamble, and it's really exciting to try to push the limits of the price as far as possible. However, when the auctioneer calls out 7 million Coppers, I see someone in the front row raise their number plate. If I don't follow at this moment, it will mean I am giving up on this cut flower. After thinking for a moment, I decide to raise my number plate.

Three people raised their number plates in this round. According to the rules of the auction, we will now make increasing bids starting from 7 million Coppers, and each bid must be at least an increase of half a million Coppers.

Someone shouts out 7.5 million Coppers right after the auctioneer explains the rules. To follow suit, I and the buyer who raised their number plate first will have to raise the bid to 8 million Coppers.
8 million Coppers... I guess that's reasonable. In addition, I'll miss out on this flower directly if I give up now, so there is room for me to struggle.
After weighing my options, I call out the price of 8 million Coppers.
The crisp sound of the mallet announces my success. The two other buyers choose to give up.
When I turn around to share my joy with Noah, she frowns and thinks for a while before talking to me.
8 million Coppers... If I want to buy it at this price, I would have made a bid earlier. Looking at the two other flowers that will be sold later on the stage, I decide to give up on this one.
{character:Auctioneer}7.5 million Coppers going once.
{character:Auctioneer}7.5 million Coppers going twice.
{character:Auctioneer}7.5 million Coppers going three times.
{character:Auctioneer}The flowing gold camellia has been sold at the price of 7.5 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.23.

The crisp sound of the mallet announces the sale of the flower. I and the other buyer don't follow the price. It looks like there's nothing wrong with my decision as everyone seems to think this flower isn't worth more than 7.5 million Coppers.

After a five-minute break, the auction for the coral red skimmia begins. It also starts at the price of 50 million Coppers, but everyone at the scene is obviously calmer this time after seeing how fast the price dropped last time.
No, I think he just doesn't want to take the blame. That way, he can make me take full responsibility if anything goes wrong!
I groan in my heart and listen to the auctioneer's price calls seriously.
The price starts off high and drops quickly like last time. When the price reaches 10 million Coppers...
After learning from my mistake last time, I decide to get it immediately this time. Also, the information Noah just gave me seems to be hinting at something.
Since it looks superior, is it possible that this means that it represents someone who has a higher status?
With this thought in mind, I decisively raise my number plate. The auctioneer looks at me and starts calling out the bid after nodding at me.
{character:Auctioneer}The coral red skimmia has been sold at the price of 10 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.17.
The crisp sound of the mallet announces my success since nobody is competing with me, but before I can share my joy with Noah, I hear a sigh next to me.

After comparing the transaction price of this flower in the last two years, I realized that there isn't much difference in the price, which means the price of this flower is quite stable, so I decide to wait for the price to fall into a suitable range.

The auctioneer continues to lower the price. To my surprise, someone raises their number plate when the price reaches 9 million Coppers this time. I wonder if the people here have been stimulated by the higher transaction price of the flowing gold camellia just now. It could also be because the flower looks better than the one last year like Noah mentioned, and some regulars might think this is a signal.
I need to consider it carefully...

I can only bid on three flower arrangements in this auction with my number plate, and I just missed out on one flower. Since the price seems to be following an increasing trend, the third flower arrangement might be even more expensive.
Kutsuji has only given me 10 million Coppers to use. Rather than failing to get the next flower arrangement, I rather take a gamble with this one, so I raise my number plate.

This time, only me and one other buyer raised our number plates. According to the rules of the auction, we will now make increasing bids starting from 9 million Coppers, and each bid must be at least an increase of half a million Coppers.
As the other buyer raised their number plate first, I get to shout out my price first this time.
{character:player}9.5 million.
{character:Auctioneer}9.5 million Coppers going once.
{character:Auctioneer}9.5 million Coppers going twice.
{character:Auctioneer}9.5 million Coppers going three times.
{character:Auctioneer}The coral red skimmia has been sold at the price of 9.5 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.17.

The crisp sound of the mallet announces my success. The other buyer chooses to give up, probably because they don't think it's worth 10 million Coppers. That's true though. If they wanted to buy it for 10 million Coppers, they could have raised their number plate earlier.
Before I can share my joy with Noah, I hear a sigh next to me.

The current price is 9 million Coppers. I'll need to raise the bid if I raise my number plate now, and the price might even end up higher than 10 million Coppers, so this isn't a good decision. I might as well give up on this one and put all my time and effort on the next flower.
{character:Auctioneer}9 million Coppers going once.
{character:Auctioneer}9 million Coppers going twice.
{character:Auctioneer}9 million Coppers going three times.
{character:Auctioneer}The coral red skimmia has been sold at the price of 9 million Coppers. Congratulations to you, Buyer No.6.

The crisp sound of the mallet announces the sale. Now I only have one option left, the snow tower peony. No matter what, I must get it for 10 million Coppers or less, or else I will have achieved nothing today.

{character:Noah}(Text message) The snow peonies in this flower arrangement are grown as a pair, and it's quite rare for them to grow to this size. According to Strix's information database, this is Countless Springs's latest flower breed, and this is the first time it is being sold in their auction.
